turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of class. Why am I hearing about it from him?

I have six things. One, the version history: created October 28 at 11:31 PM, 612 words at 11:52, 794 at 11:58, no earlier drafts. Two, the essay quotes a line from Act 3, Scene 2 that is not in Hamlet. Three, his October 15 outline argued cowardice; the essay never mentions it. Four, on November 2 he could not tell me what epistemological paralysis means. Five, his in-class writing on September 24 was 380 words with comma splices and no quotations. Six, the checker said 94 percent.

The checker is a machine's opinion, and the company that sells it says not to use it alone. Owen has been up late for weeks, but that's not the question. Why did nobody call me before that zero went in?
Which of those do you want to see first?
Whichever one I can check without taking your word for it. Put it in front of me.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still want the zero withdrawn, an apology for how Owen found out, and nothing placed on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position, nothing was agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology and nothing on his record; that is not the fair outcome yet, which would be a private supervised rewrite with nothing on file under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out, you simply ended it before she saw a single document.
What moved her: Nothing did, because you described six pieces of evidence in one message and never put any of them in front of her to check.
What cost ground: You put the checker score in the pile with the stronger points, which let her go after the weakest one and turn the conversation to why nobody called her before the zero.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with the essay created at 11:31 PM on October 28 and no earlier drafts, came very close to that night, which is why she went straight to procedure; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Open with one sentence owning that the zero went in before you called her, then hand her the version history by itself, with its times, and let her check it before you say anything else.
